Neha Joshi is a Class 9 teacher who loves storytelling. She has been teaching since January, when she was nine and taught for eight years at the school. Her favourite part of the day is telling her stories in class.
She writes that every child learns something new each week, so being kind to everyone helps too. Neha Joshi enjoys sharing her love with others.
The children have a wonderful time together during the holidays.

A tiny grey elephant named Gopal was the biggest and most feared of all animals. He had no way to escape from a mouse, so he hid behind a tree in the forest.

One day, a little girl named Chloe came walking through the trees with her father. She saw him hiding and asked, "What are you doing?"
"I'm afraid," said Gopal.

Chloe smiled kindly at his fear. She crouched down and began to tell funny stories about how she found the mice. Soon, the other elephants joined in too. They laughed together until they were tired.

At night, the family drove to a quiet town. The car was old and slow, with dark windows and a silent road. A man named Mr. Rao said it would be hard at first. "I can't do that," he said.
"Then I will help you," said the driver. He showed them how to turn on the radio or ask someone in charge to look over their shoulder. They listened for claps of songs. Soon they were laughing and smiling together.
The next morning, the car stopped working. Dad took out his phone and called 911. His team waited outside the door. When the lights came back, everyone got out safely.

Mira sat in her room, and she was so tired that the moon seemed to yawn. She closed her eyes and began to dream.
In the morning, Mira woke up with a smile on her face. The stars were out above the garden wall, and they twinkled like tiny dots. "Goodnight," said Mira softly.

The next day, Mira went back to bed. But this time, something strange happened: the moon had yawned all night! It was very loud, but Mira did not mind. She smiled and fell asleep right away.

Mira had never seen a kite before, and she was excited. She ran to the roof with her bucket of water and tried to reach it. The wind blew hard, but she did not give up. Finally, she found one in the corner of her room. It was long and thin, and looked like a tiny green kite. Mira held it gently while she climbed back down. Her father clapped his hands. "Good job," he said. "Now let's see how far you can throw." They threw the kite together at the top of the roof, and Mira watched from there until it came out again.

When the old man came to our house, he was haunted by a strange noise. He stood in front of his door with a long black beard and held out his hand. "Who are you?"
"I am Mr. Bose." The voice said, "Come here, I have something that will make you laugh."
The boy looked up from his book. It was only an old woman who had come home late at night. She smiled kindly and gave him a small box of sweets.

She sat down beside him and began to tell stories about her childhood. They laughed until she fell asleep. When he woke up, it was dark outside. He felt scared but stayed close.

He walked slowly through the hall, holding on to every word. Then he heard someone calling for help. A girl named Mrs. Pillai stepped into the room. She saw him standing alone in front of the wall, trembling. She knelt down and asked what was wrong. He told her everything.

Mrs. Pillai listened without judging. She thanked him warmly and offered her some sweets. After that, they ate together at the gate, and Mr. Bose went back to sleep.

At the school gate, a boy named Mr. Rao was waiting for his turn to walk home from the gate. He had just finished his maths homework and was too tired to even look at the wall. The puppy followed him home, still strayed by the door.

Mr. Rao's friend Mrs. Pillai noticed he looked tired and came over with her bag of sweets. "You can have one," she said kindly. She gave him half a biscuit and kept it in two slices.

He ate it all up. Then he walked slowly down the lane, holding out his hand. It felt like being part of the group.

Isaac was a boy who tried to cook dinner for his parents. He burned rice, and the family cooked it in a pan on the stove. When the rice was ready, he took out the pot and started stirring. The smell of hot water filled the kitchen. His father laughed and tasted it too. They ate together while they watched the smoke drift down from the ceiling. It felt like a treat everyone shared.

Mira had a goldfish named Mira. She was only three years old and very curious about the world, so she asked her parents to take her on an adventure.
One day, they went for a walk in the park near their house. The sky turned grey, and Mira heard strange sounds. Then she saw something glimmering under a tree. It was a tiny silver fish!
"Hello," said Mira. "What are you?"
The little fish looked up at her with big eyes. "I am a magic fish."
Mira gasped. "How can I help?" she wondered.
Her father gently scooped out some of its food, and Mira watched it swim away. After that, Mira waved goodbye as they walked home through the foggy morning.

Every morning, the children opened their tiffin boxes and found nothing inside. They looked under every box, but it was nowhere to be seen.
"Where are you?" asked one child, who had eaten his lunch. "I can't see them."

The teacher knelt down and began a small game of hiding in each box. The children laughed so hard that they forgot how long to remember.
After ten minutes, the teacher said, "You have been very good at this. You always find what you hide."

At the end of the day, the class learned about the lost tiffin box. It still sits on the table with its stories.

The parrot that could repeat was called the blue one. Every time it repeated a word, he said "twelve". The other birds laughed and flew away. His family's stomach felt funny. He sat on the grass with his head in a loop of silence. Then he heard a tiny voice say, "Hello."
"Who are you?" asked the parrot.

"I am the blue one," replied the other bird.

He looked around but saw nothing. He thought for a moment, then spoke again. "You are the blue one!"

A small green frog hopped out from behind a bush. She smiled at him. They talked until her tail brushed against her back. When she had finished, they both agreed to meet every day after that.

Every morning, the grandfather rode his bicycle to school. He had never seen anyone ride it before. His daughter held him in her seat and looked out at the road with big eyes.

One day, a little girl named Chloe came along. She was only three years old but very brave. She asked if she could try on the chain. The father said no, because he wanted her to learn how to balance. But she begged anyway.

Chloe sat down beside him, held the chain as if it were hers. Then she tried again slowly, one step at a time. At last, she did it! She wobbled, nearly the same way she always does. Her mother clapped and cheered for her.

Every evening, the little girl named Kia sat on her balcony with a cup of tea. She had been waiting for this train all week and was very excited. Her uncle's old radio played back from his trip, but she only heard music.
One day, the train stopped at a station. The driver opened the door, looked around, then turned to the window. He saw a boy sitting in a plastic chair with a bag next to him. His name was Mr. Bose.
"Hi," said Kia. "I miss my train."
Mr. Bose smiled kindly. "You can come along if you like," he said. They walked together down the track, holding hands.
Kia felt sad that her train ride had ended so fast. But she knew it would be another long journey, because she loved trains.

The monkey was a very clever monkey. He lived in the forest and had many friends, but he always wanted to be the one who knew everything. One day, he saw the crocodile eating leaves from a tree. The monkey thought of an idea.
He asked his friend, a wise old owl named Mr. Hoot, for help. "Mr. Hoot," said the monkey. "I want to know how much I weigh." Mr. Hoot smiled gently. "That is not something you can do alone."
"But it would make him proud," said the monkey. "If we all helped each other, we could learn even more."
Hoot agreed. "You are right," he said. They decided to ask their teacher, Mr. Keeper, about what they ate. The next morning, they found the river's source. It was full of fish that the monkeys had caught.
They thanked the animals and ran home with fresh water. From then on, they shared food every time they went out to play.

The snake lived in a big green forest. Every morning it watched the ants march around, and every night it made sure to leave them alone. One day, while walking through the grass, it found something shiny. It was an old, golden key. The snake picked it up with its long neck and carried it home.
Every evening, the snake would go back to watch the ants march by. Then, one afternoon, it put the key into its special box under its bed. That night, the snake slept until noon, and when it woke up, it had opened the door of its secret hiding place. Inside were tiny toys that belonged to all the animals who lived there.

The lion lived in a forest and carpenter Kala had been working there for years. One day, he came to the door of his house with a long trunk full of tools. He was very careful not to hurt anyone.
Kala looked up from her toolbox. "What are you doing?" she asked. The lion said, "I'm looking for something." She thought about it carefully before deciding.

She took out a small box and began to cut through it. It was hard at first but soon enough, she found what she needed: a hammer. When she handed him the hammer, he felt proud.

He thanked her and ran off into the sunset.

A jackal named Kafi was the king of the forest. He had a long, golden coat and a big black hat that glowed in the sun. Every morning he would wake up early to make sure every tree was greener.
One day, a small brown rabbit came hopping by. "I like your crown," said Kafi. The rabbit looked at it for a moment before saying, "Thank you."
Kafi smiled. Then he hopped away into the mist.
The next morning, when Kafi woke up, his crown was gone! A little girl picked it up and ran home with her mother. She put it on her head as a special memory of her grandfather's old days.

When the giant waves came down to the sea, he was on a boat with two sailors. They pushed him out of the water and threw his arms around him like birds. He laughed so hard that they fell asleep in the sand.

One day, a little girl named Kala heard from the side. She ran up to the boat and saw Hanuman. "Why are you here?" she asked.
"Because I am your friend," said Hanuman.

The captain smiled kindly at her question. "We have been waiting for someone who will come."
Kala nodded. Then she gently pulled him back into the boat. The crew waved goodbye until he reached the shore.

Arjuna was a bird of the forest. He saw it in every tree and every branch, and he knew its name. One day, Arjuna flew down to him with his eyes wide open.
"What is your name?" asked the bird.

"My name is Bhairav," said Arjun. "I am an old friend from high up."
The bird blinked. Then Bhairavi flapped his wings. The wind blew through the trees like a soft breeze.
"You are my best friend," said Arjun.

They sat on the branches together for a while. Arjuna hummed as they talked. When he came back, he had seen many birds around him.

He told Bhairavi that he had never felt so happy. They hugged each other tightly.

After that, they stayed friends forever.

Alice fell down the rabbit hole when she was five, and it felt like a very big fall. She landed on her knee in pain, and then she saw that one of her fingers had fallen out.
She ran to get help from her mother, who put a small band around her finger. The doctor said Alice needed an operation called an x-ray.
After that, Alice stayed with her friends for years. But after that, every time she went to play again, the hurt seemed bigger than before. Her friend Alice told everyone about the rabbit hole.

Tia was three and a half years old when she heard the puppy cry. She ran to her grandmother's room, holding it in her arms.

"Mummy," said Tia softly. "I found him."

Her mother smiled kindly at first. Then she knelt down beside him. "He is very small," she said gently.

She named his name, then gave him one of her own puppies. He sniffed and held it close. They walked home together, with Tia feeling warm inside.

Ravi, a boy named Ravi was playing with his red ball in the park when he saw a girl named Sana. She had lost her blue ball and looked very sad.
"Hi," said Ravi. "I have an old red ball. Do you want to play?"
Sana nodded. They played catch together on the grass. The sun shone down on them as they ran around.
After a while, Sana's eyes grew heavy. "My arm hurts." she cried. Ravi felt bad for her. He remembered that he had left it near the bench every day after school. So he went over and gave her his red ball.
Sana smiled. She thanked him and asked if she could ask again another time. Ravi told her about the other children who were looking at their balls too. They laughed until they heard someone calling them names.

Bird B. He had never flown before, and he was scared of the sky. His wings were heavy with air.
One day, a girl named Mina found him on her balcony. She held out her hand for him to hold. "You can do it," she said.

He took a deep breath. Then he flapped his wings as fast as he could. The wind pushed them up into the sky. Birds flew above the trees.

Mina watched from the window. When birds came down, they landed on their own feathers. They looked like tiny toys.
"I'll teach you," she said.

She gave him a small feather each. It felt special. Birds came back every time.

Kabir and Khaza were sitting on the floor of their classroom, eating lunch together. Kabir said something that made him feel sad. He wanted to share his sandwich with her but he had no lunch left.

One day, a new girl named Zoya came in. She sat down beside them and asked if she could have half of her sandwich. They shared it without asking for anything. Zoya was kind and gave back some of her own.

The two friends ate happily all afternoon. When they finished, Zoya thanked them both and promised never to leave her food alone again.

A cat named Meena was always afraid of the rain. One day, she heard a strange noise in her home: thunder. She ran to her bed and hid under the covers.
 Her mother came into the room with a torch. "Look," said her mother, holding up something shiny. It looked like a tiny drum. The little girl peeked out from behind the curtain.
She saw that it had no sound. Then she noticed that one drop of water dripped on the floor. It was wet and slippery. She picked it up and held it close.

"It's okay," said her mother. "You can make it feel better." They sat together while the storm passed. When the sky opened again, Meena felt calmer.
